scenes.visual: Title card: A Ramp to a Bound.

scenes.tts: When should a brain stop collecting evidence and commit to an answer?
scenes.visual: The fan of tally traces from chapter one, still climbing. The question appears as on-screen text.
scenes.narration: When should a brain stop collecting evidence and commit to an answer?

scenes.tts: The evidence comes from M T, the middle temporal area, whose neurons are tuned to direction. What adds it up?
scenes.caption: The evidence comes from MT, the middle temporal area, whose neurons are tuned to direction. What adds it up?
scenes.visual: A monkey brain with area MT highlighted, small tuning curves above a few MT neurons. Arrows flow from MT toward a box labelled: adds it up?
scenes.narration: The evidence comes from MT, the middle temporal area, whose neurons are tuned to direction. What adds it up?

scenes.tts: The simplest rule is a bound. Keep adding until the running total reaches a set level, then act.
scenes.visual: A horizontal line labelled bound is drawn across the top of a graph.
scenes.narration: The simplest rule is a bound. Keep adding until the running total reaches a set level, then act.

scenes.tts: Picture a graph, with time along the bottom and the running total up the side.
scenes.visual: Axes are labelled: time since dots appeared (horizontal), running total (vertical).
scenes.narration: Picture a graph, with time along the bottom and the running total up the side.

scenes.tts: The total drifts upward. Stronger motion means a steeper drift, so the total reaches the bound sooner.
scenes.visual: Two smooth lines climb from the same start: a steep one for strong motion hits the bound early; a shallow one for weak motion hits it later. Label: drift.
scenes.narration: The total drifts upward. Stronger motion means a steeper drift, so the total reaches the bound sooner.

scenes.tts: Noise adds a wobble. On some trials the total arrives early, and on others late.
scenes.visual: A wobbly trace climbs to the bound. Several more wobbly traces reach the bound at different times; small tick marks on the time axis spread out.
scenes.narration: Noise adds a wobble. On some trials the total arrives early, and on others late.

scenes.tts: For a choice between two directions, draw a second bound below the start, for the other answer.
scenes.visual: A second horizontal line appears below the starting point, labelled: other choice.
scenes.narration: For a choice between two directions, draw a second bound below the start, for the other answer.

scenes.tts: On weak-motion trials, the wobble sometimes carries the total to the wrong bound. That is an error.
scenes.visual: A weak-motion trace wanders and ends on the lower bound. It flashes orange. Label: error.
scenes.narration: On weak-motion trials, the wobble sometimes carries the total to the wrong bound. That is an error.

scenes.tts: This is a drift-to-bound model.
scenes.visual: Title card: drift-to-bound model. On screen only: Without noise: time to bound = (bound − start) ÷ drift; reaction time = latency + time to bound + motor delay.
scenes.narration: This is a drift-to-bound model.

scenes.tts: Suppose some neuron held this running total. What would its firing do just before the eye moves?
scenes.visual: On-screen card with the question. Empty axes: firing rate against time, with a marker for the eye movement.
scenes.narration: Suppose some neuron held this running total. What would its firing do just before the eye moves?

scenes.visual: The question stays on screen; a small countdown ring runs.

scenes.tts: On trials choosing the target this neuron represents, it should climb, more steeply when the motion is strong. And it should reach about the same level just before the eye moves. The other choice has a different endpoint.
scenes.visual: Predicted lines, labelled: choices toward the neuron's response-field target, climb at different slopes and meet at one high level just before the eye-movement marker. Fainter lines for the other choice head toward the lower bound instead.
scenes.narration: On trials choosing the target this neuron represents, it should climb, more steeply when the motion is strong. And it should reach about the same level just before the eye moves. The other choice has a different endpoint.

scenes.tts: Now the data. Roitman and Shadlen recorded from the lateral intraparietal area, or L I P, in rhesus monkeys.
scenes.caption: Now the data. Roitman and Shadlen recorded from the lateral intraparietal area, or LIP, in rhesus monkeys.
scenes.visual: A monkey brain with area LIP highlighted in the parietal lobe. Label: LIP, lateral intraparietal area.
scenes.narration: Now the data. Roitman and Shadlen recorded from the lateral intraparietal area, or LIP, in rhesus monkeys.

scenes.tts: Its neurons fire before an eye movement to a target in their response field.
scenes.visual: One of the two choice targets glows inside a shaded patch labelled response field.
scenes.narration: Its neurons fire before an eye movement to a target in their response field.

scenes.tts: Averaged over many trials, the lines lie together for the first two hundred milliseconds or so.
scenes.caption: Averaged over many trials, the lines lie together for the first 200 milliseconds or so.
scenes.visual: Their figure, redrawn: firing rate against time from motion onset, one line per motion strength, overlapping for about the first 200 ms.
scenes.narration: Averaged over many trials, the lines lie together for the first 200 milliseconds or so.

scenes.tts: Then they ramp. The ramp is steeper for stronger motion when the monkey chose the target in the response field.
scenes.visual: The lines fan apart and climb; the strongest-motion line is steepest. Label: averages, not single trials.
scenes.narration: Then they ramp. The ramp is steeper for stronger motion when the monkey chose the target in the response field.

scenes.tts: Lined up to the eye movement, the firing reaches about the same rate, whatever the motion strength. The authors read this as an apparent threshold.
scenes.visual: The same lines realigned to the saccade converge at one level just before it. A dashed line marks the common level.
scenes.narration: Lined up to the eye movement, the firing reaches about the same rate, whatever the motion strength. The authors read this as an apparent threshold.

scenes.tts: These are averages over many trials. Single trials may look different.
scenes.visual: A small card: averages over many trials; see Going deeper.
scenes.narration: These are averages over many trials. Single trials may look different.

scenes.tts: Noise also changes the timing. At weak motion, the wobble carries many trials to a bound early, sometimes the wrong one.
scenes.visual: A table appears silently: noiseless reaction times 370, 670 and 1,870 ms beside noisy ones of about 370, 590 and 700 ms, at 51.2%, 12.8% and 3.2% coherence. Label: invented numbers, from one model.
scenes.narration: Noise also changes the timing. At weak motion, the wobble carries many trials to a bound early, sometimes the wrong one.

scenes.tts: With two bounds, you never wait forever. So mean times are shorter than a noiseless model predicts.
scenes.visual: The table stays on screen. Weak-motion traces hit both bounds early; some end on the wrong one.
scenes.narration: With two bounds, you never wait forever. So mean times are shorter than a noiseless model predicts.

scenes.tts: Now move both bounds farther from the start. Choices get slower, and more accurate wherever there is net motion.
scenes.visual: The upper and lower bounds move farther from the start. The traces take longer to reach them.
scenes.narration: Now move both bounds farther from the start. Choices get slower, and more accurate wherever there is net motion.

scenes.tts: The slowing is biggest at weak motion, where the wobble, not the drift, sets the time to the bound.
scenes.visual: Strong-motion traces are barely delayed; weak-motion traces are delayed a lot. Their arrival times are highlighted.
scenes.narration: The slowing is biggest at weak motion, where the wobble, not the drift, sets the time to the bound.

scenes.tts: A decision can be a running total that stops at a bound. The bound sets the trade between speed and accuracy.
scenes.visual: Takeaway card: a running total that stops at a bound; the bound trades speed for accuracy.
scenes.narration: A decision can be a running total that stops at a bound. The bound sets the trade between speed and accuracy.
